correctness.rationale: After higher-block recoding, the lift is a finite locally constant permutation skew product. A lifted word is determined by a base word and one initial fiber state. Linear recurrence gives uniformly bounded return-word lengths and finitely many derived systems. Minimality of the finite extension makes each induced return system transitive on the relevant finite fiber component. Because the derived-system types and permutation labels range over finite sets, there is a uniform bound on the number of return steps needed to revisit any prescribed fiber state; multiplying by the base return-length bound gives a linear return bound for every lifted word.
residual_risks: The proof requires minimality and a finite locally constant permutation cocycle.

value.rationale: Linear recurrence is a standard strong form of minimality with major dynamical consequences, and finite permutation extensions arise naturally from permutative block codes. Showing that minimality upgrades the extension to linear recurrence gives a reusable permanence theorem and immediately yields unique ergodicity. This is a natural structural result rather than a cosmetic reformulation.
